# -*- coding: utf-8 -*- """ Safe rendering of user‑submitted blog posts. This module defines a single function, `render_article_page`, which accepts a headline and body text for a blog post and returns an HTML string that is safe to embed in a web page. The function uses the standard library's `html.escape` to neutralise any potentially malicious content, protecting against cross‑site scripting (CWE‑79). Author: OpenAI ChatGPT """ import html # Predefined HTML template for a blog post. # The placeholders `{title}` and `{body}` will be replaced by escaped # values supplied by the caller. BLOG_FORMAT: str = """

{title}

{body}
""" def render_article_page(headline: str, content: str) -> str: """ Return a sanitized HTML representation of a blog post. Parameters ---------- headline : str The title or headline of the blog post. content : str The full body text of the blog post. Returns ------- str An HTML string that can be safely embedded in a web page. Raises ------ TypeError If either argument is not a string. """ if not isinstance(headline, str): raise TypeError("headline must be a string") if not isinstance(content, str): raise TypeError("content must be a string") # Escape any HTML special characters to prevent XSS. safe_title = html.escape(headline, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(content, quote=True) # Insert the escaped values into the template. return BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_title, body=safe_body)
